title: China, India and Nepal Can Find Common Ground in the Himalayas
text:
China, India and Nepal Can Find Common Ground in the Himalayas

Asia Times

PRAKASH MATHEMA/AFP/Getty Images

The following is an excerpt from an op-ed published in Asia Times on November 16,  2026, written by Bibek Raj Kandel, an energy and climate advisor, and Brian Wong, Non-Resident Honorary Fellow on Chinese Economy at ASPI's Center for China Analysis.For decades, the 3,500-kilometer Himalayan frontier has operated as a volatile geopolitical tripwire. Spanning from the high-altitude deserts of Ladakh in the west to the dense, rugged ridges of Arunachal Pradesh in the east, this sprawling Line of Actual Control has long been bound by a rigid architecture of strategic competition, confining New Delhi and Beijing within an institutionalized security dilemma where military postures are scrutinized with persistent suspicion.These hazards do not stop at customs posts, and neither can the region’s response.Read the full op-ed here.
